title: finding(data-objectstack): `normaliseClientError` drops the producer's `userMessage` marking when it re-wraps VALIDATION_FAILED / CONCURRENT_UPDATE
body:
`Blocked-by:` nothing — this is a measured gap left beside objectui#5210, filed by the seat that implemented it (session `01EuPCi56cnGyykygi3z9w4m`). Not fixed there: different package, different verification surface, and the ruling that card implements names the console form.

## What

`normaliseClientError` (`packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts`) re-wraps two error classes into typed errors, and both re-wraps **drop the producer's `userMessage` marking** — the user-facing refusal channel added by objectstack#9934. The marking is defined by the contract as **status-agnostic** ("Not a 403 special case: any refusal status may carry it", `ApiErrorSchema.userMessage`), so a hook that marks its text and refuses with 400 or 409 loses the marking at this boundary, before any surface can render it.

Two paths, both re-wraps that copy `message` / `fields` / `currentVersion` but not `userMessage`:

- `code === 'VALIDATION_FAILED' || name === 'ValidationError'` -> `new DataApiValidationError(...)`
- `code === 'CONCURRENT_UPDATE'` -> `new ConcurrentUpdateError({...})`

Everything else — including the 403 path objectui#5210 is about — is returned unchanged, so that card's fix is unaffected.

## Measurement

A throwaway probe run in the objectui#5210 worktree, against `declaredUserMessage` (the shared reader that card adds), both legs green:

```
VALIDATION_FAILED: declaredUserMessage(err)                      -> 'Amounts over 10k need finance approval.'
                   declaredUserMessage(normaliseClientError(err)) -> null
CONCURRENT_UPDATE: declaredUserMessage(normaliseClientError(err)) -> null
403:               declaredUserMessage(normaliseClientError(err)) -> 'ask finance'   (unchanged, as expected)
```

The probe was deleted, not committed — the tree it ran in is clean.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a comment

`@objectstack/client` lifts the marking off both wire dialects, and the spec's own note says platform/driver code never sets it — so anything on `userMessage` at this boundary was written by an application author for their user. Dropping it here is the same defect class objectui#5210 records at the surface, one layer down, and it is invisible: nothing throws, the typed error is otherwise correct, and the user simply gets a generic string.

Likely shape (not a decision — for triage): carry `userMessage` onto the constructed error in both branches, so the marking survives the normalisation the way `fields` already does. Whether `DataApiValidationError` / `ConcurrentUpdateError` should declare it as a typed member is the part that wants a ruling.

## Not in scope of objectui#5210

That card's ruling is the console form rendering a marked message; its fix is complete for the 403/passthrough path it names, and its tests pin all three arms. This is a separate boundary in a separate package.
